text:
alex: opened a tiny PR that adds an optional 'burst hint' header so SDKs can signal short-lived high-cost requests: https://git.internal/redwood/sdk/pulls/1201

sam: quick semantics check: is this advisory only or will the server treat it as quota consumption?

alex: advisory only. server quotas unchanged. header name: `X-RW-Burst-Hint: <int>` where int is estimated units for the request. SDK default = off; opt-in via constructor: `new RedwoodClient({ burstHint: { enabled: true } })`.

maria: console/ingest note: we'll add `burst_hint` to the raw event schema and tag events that include it. for visualization we should smooth these signals so dashboards don't jump. proposal: compute an EMA (alpha=0.2) per-route and show both raw and smoothed lines.

tom: ops wants a canary. please do not bake rollout percentages into SDK. server-side routing should mark canary accounts; SDKs only send the hint.

alex: agreed, SDK will not carry any canary metadata. we'll add a small logger line when header is emitted: `logger.info("burst-hint sent", { units })`. unit tests included.

sam: UX asks: default dashboard behavior should remain unchanged. add an opt-in overlay called "Client burst hints (opt-in)" and an adoption tile showing percent of requests with hints.

maria: ingestion will also record `metering_schema_version` so we can evolve without breaking backfills. backfill plan: for first 21 days, treat missing header as unknown and leave server-only aggregates intact. customers can opt-out of backfill via feature flag.

ci-bot: CI: unit tests passed, integration flaky timeout retried, succeeded. PR 1201 merged to main.

tom: docs: add explicit sentence in quotas page: "Server-side quota enforcement is authoritative; client burst hints are advisory and used for estimation only." I'll add the changelog entry.

alex: thanks all. next steps: @maria (dashboard smoothing + overlay), @tom (docs/changelog), @sam (ops canary list).
